commons.robots: commons.wikimedia.org/robots.txt disallows /w/ for a generic crawler. The Wikimedia Foundation API Usage Guidelines allow identified use of /w/api.php.
commons.terms: Calls use BioCatHeadlinesBot/1.0 (https://biocat.ai/; contact@biocat.ai), one at a time, maxlag=5, and at most 20 calls a run. Files are kept only for CC0, public domain, CC BY, or CC BY-SA, with an author credit.

openverse.terms: The API also publishes anonymous rate limits (20/minute, 200/day). That conflict is enough to leave the client off. Set OPENVERSE_IMAGES=1 to call it. CC0 and CC BY would be the only licences kept.

nasa.robots: images-api.nasa.gov/robots.txt returns 404, so there is no disallow rule. api.nasa.gov/robots.txt is also 404.
nasa.terms: NASA images are U.S. government works unless the record says otherwise. Logos, insignia, and images of identifiable people are skipped, as is anything credited as a courtesy or under a third-party copyright.

flickr-niaid.robots: www.flickr.com/robots.txt and api.flickr.com/robots.txt both say User-agent: * / Disallow: /.
flickr-niaid.terms: Automated access is disallowed, so NIAID Flickr is not queried and no photo licence field is read from it.

nci-visuals.robots: visualsonline.cancer.gov did not resolve on 2026-11-17, so robots.txt and the terms page could not be read.
nci-visuals.terms: No replacement NCI Visuals API with a per-image rights field was found. The source is not queried. Copyrighted NCI items would have been skipped anyway.

cdc-phil.robots: wwwn.cdc.gov/phil/robots.txt returns 404. www.cdc.gov/robots.txt does not disallow /phil/.
cdc-phil.terms: PHIL search is an ASP.NET postback, not a stable API. A detail page repeats a site-wide copyright notice and does not mark that individual image as public domain, so the required per-image rights check cannot pass. The source is not queried.
